P1.evidence: Application acknowledged but not read back — 'I've read through your application, so I have a bit of a head start' — with no specifics reflected, so P1a is a weaker variant. Four-part frame delivered cleanly: 'where you're at in your fitness journey, where you're trying to get to, what's kind of missing in between. And then from there, we can map out what a potential coaching program could [look like].' Frame agreement taken and given: 'That all sound good?' / 'Sure, sure. Let's go.' Open question run verbatim: 'what do you feel we could potentially help you with today? Give me a bit of an overview.'

P2.evidence: The strongest baseline in this batch — every check asked directly rather than volunteered. 'How old are you and what's your height and weight?' produced 34, 5'10", 180 lb. Work asked and the desk-bound qualifier established: 'What do you do for work, man?' / 'I'm mostly sitting.' Health conditions asked and then properly pursued — 'Any injuries or pain or any other medical conditions that would interfere with working out at all?' followed by 'Are we pretty hard above or what? What's the scoop?' on the cholesterol, which is what surfaced the full family cardiac history. Injuries covered with duration (calf two weeks, shoulder chronic from boxing). Training week asked twice and pinned to actual sessions: 'How many times a week are we swimming versus running right now?' Results probed: 'why do we feel like we're not at our body fat goals yet?' and 'Have you gotten your body fat percentage tested at all?' Full day of eating taken. Sleep asked and root-caused — 'how's sleep' / 'bad' / 'do we know why' — and energy asked in the same run.

P3.evidence: Surface layer is approximated rather than run — 'What's the ultimate goal in your fitness right now?' substitutes for the one-thing-you'd-change question, though it did pin a number (under 12 percent), and the something-physical-you-can't-do question was never asked. The vision exercise stands in for P3e: 'six months from now, abracadabra, you know, Alakazam... what do you want life and fitness to actually look like, man?' The deep layer is excellent. Bridge run twice, the second time as a challenge: 'how important is it actually to shed the body fat for you? Because... it doesn't seem like it's been that big of a priority.' Who-else asked directly — 'what happens to the kids then?' — and the prospect produced the answer himself: 'I am the leader of this household. if that's what they see, then that's what they'll do.' Driven all the way to legacy and generational pattern. Reflected back and confirmed: 'the reason you're going to say no to moving forward with something like Trevor's coaching is going to be the exact same thing that's [messing] you up in the rest of your life', which the prospect accepted — 'you've quickly identified probably the root cause of my struggles.'

P4.evidence: All six ran. 'What else have you tried to start losing some of this weight, man?' produced the smoking cutback, better dinners and roughly five pounds lost. Timeline probed — 'how long have you been thinking about like, man, I know I should probably be a little bit more on top of this' — and the trigger isolated: 'what changed the last month or two', which surfaced the blood work. Root cause driven to the actual blocker rather than the presenting one: 'what are you running away from when you turn to weed? Because there's always something that we don't want to feel.' The prospect named the gap repeatedly in his own words — 'I probably don't eat well', 'you're probably right, I'd like it to be more of a priority than I've made it', 'I fixed the habits'. P4f landed hardest against the self-sufficiency objection: 'historical evidence has shown us that you've not been able to make a change by yourself up to this point.'

P5.evidence: Textbook. 'what's the next two, three, five years look like for you?' answered 'Probably stay the same, or get worse, and or get put on a statin.' Devil's advocate run properly — 'why not just kind of keep going the easy route? Because again, you don't like it now, you don't like it then either.' Settle-for asked explicitly: 'is that something that you're willing to settle for?' Answer: 'No. No, it's not. That's why I'm here.' Line in the sand asked and taken: 'are we feeling like it's time to draw a line in the sand and actually get this stuff handled?' / 'Yes. I draw the line in the sand.'

P6.evidence: Neither scripted commitment question was asked. P6a in particular was left on the table at the exact moment it was needed: the prospect said 'in three months, I probably won't even need you guys', which is a direct denial of the premise P6a tests, and the rep argued with it instead of asking it. But P6c was executed better than anywhere else in this batch. He had a verbal yes on the line in the sand, judged it hollow — 'There's still, I can still feel there's some hesitations towards actually making a full commitment' — and refused to advance: 'until we actually talk about and address this, I wouldn't even actually consider offering you to come and join Trevor's coaching.' He returned to consequence and pattern work rather than presenting, which is exactly what the script requires.

P11.evidence: No close was attempted and the offer was deliberately withheld. No price, agreement, onboarding call or Skool link arose in 67 minutes.

objection_plays.detail: The substance of 'I need to think about it' arrived as a scheduling request at 01:01:25 — 'How about we talk again in a week? That way I spend a full week to feel the feelings that I don't want to feel tonight.' The rep correctly identified it as avoidance and did not accept it, which is the spirit of 'Thinking isn't the problem. Deciding is.' But none of the scripted moves ran: no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal?', no 'what's actually coming up that's preventing you from getting started?', no future-self question. And it did not close out — the prospect deferred ('I'll take your recommendation') rather than deciding, and the rep himself immediately predicted a cancellation.

Fear and doubt surfaced twice — 'Feels a little nerve-wracking, huh?' / 'It does. Commitment is like that', and again as resistance to destroying the gummies: 'is there a way I can move forward without throwing them away?' The rep worked it hard with unscripted material: the hidden-pill relapse story, his own video-game and addiction history, and a BRIDGE-equivalent in 'it's uncomfortable for like a month and you're like, okay, I'm fine.' None of the scripted moves ran — no certainty question, no pleasure-versus-pain, no plane analogy, no 'how will you know if you never actually try?'

A self-sufficiency objection with no scripted play: 'If I do commit to a change, I do make a change, commit to it, in three months, I probably won't even need you guys.' This is not price and not a cheaper competitor — it is the claim that coaching itself is unnecessary once the decision is made, and it is the natural objection from a genuinely capable prospect. Proposed label: self_sufficiency_no_coach_needed. The rep improvised well and got agreement ('That's true'), but this is a real gap in the script alongside the two already documented.

A clinical decision was raised and turned into sales leverage with no scripted guardrail. The prospect said 'I probably should be medicated. I would like to avoid it... I don't want to be on the statin.' The rep adopted the statin as the consequence of failure rather than staying neutral — 'what's the next two, three, five years look like for you?' / 'get put on a statin' — and never suggested he follow his physician's advice. The script has no play, and no guardrail, for a prospect weighing a prescribed medication against a coaching programme.

notes: Phases 2 through 5 are the best work in this batch — the baseline is complete, every fact was asked for rather than volunteered, and the consequence frame produced a genuine line in the sand. The problem is what happened after P6c. Refusing to present was the right call; spending the next twenty minutes running an unlicensed addiction intervention, including instructing the prospect to leave the call and destroy his cannabis, was not, and the prospect named it twice — 'you bullied me into making a change' and 'Are you a therapist?' Coach the rep to convert a correct P6c hold into a rebooked call, not into therapy. Also note that a 67-minute call produced no price, no pillars and a next step the rep openly expected to be cancelled.
